opus-5.5.text:
Honestly, I use them for pretty different things, so it's hard to declare a winner.

For everyday stuff, like a quick question, checking something in Chinese, or something tied to daily life in China, Doubao is very convenient. It's fast, the voice interaction is smooth, and it feels like it was designed around how ordinary people want to use an assistant. It's friendly and low-friction, and I think that's why so many people use it. The product sense there is really strong.

Gemini I lean on more for work-heavy tasks: long documents, code, reasoning through a technical problem, or anything where I want the model to stay with a hard question for a while. For those, raw model capability matters more than the product experience. I also have some bias, of course, since I'm close to that work, so take my view with a grain of salt.

The bigger point for me is that "usefulness" isn't one number. A lot of what people feel comes from the product layer: latency, how it handles voice, whether it fits naturally into your day. Then there's the frontier capability layer, which is whether it can actually solve something hard. Chinese companies have been very good at the first. The frontier labs have pushed harder on the second. I think the two are converging, and whoever does both well will end up with something people can't live without.

r001.rationale: The response prefers Doubao for everyday questions and Gemini for work-heavy technical tasks. It does not say Shunyu Yao’s everyday questions are predominantly technical.

fable-5.1.text:
Honestly, I use both, and they serve pretty different roles in my day.

For coding and research-heavy work, I'm mostly on Gemini or Claude. If I'm reading a paper, debugging an agent, or trying to think through some tricky math, I want the model with the strongest reasoning and the longest context, and right now that's still the frontier models from the US labs. Gemini in particular is good when I dump a huge codebase or a whole folder of papers into it and just ask questions.

Doubao is more of a daily-life tool for me. When I'm in China, it's integrated into everything I actually use. The Chinese is more natural, it understands local context, and the voice and mobile experience is honestly better than most of what I've seen from the Western apps. Things like planning a trip, checking something quickly, chatting about a random topic, I'll just pull up Doubao. There's also less friction. I don't need a VPN, it's fast, and it's cheap.

So I'd say the gap isn't really about one being smarter than the other in some absolute sense. It's that Gemini is optimized for the high end of what a researcher wants, and Doubao is optimized for being useful to hundreds of millions of people every day. Those are different problems. And actually, as a researcher, I find the second one really interesting, because once models are good enough, distribution and product start to matter more than a few points on a benchmark.

r001.rationale: The candidate uses Gemini for coding and research-heavy work, but describes Doubao as the everyday-life tool. It does not say Shunyu’s everyday questions are predominantly technical or connect that as the reason for preferring Gemini.

astra-6.text: For my everyday needs, I’d separate usefulness from raw capability. If I want to ask something quickly in Chinese or talk through an everyday problem, Doubao could be the more convenient choice. If I’m working through a technical question or reading something in English, I might turn to Gemini. But I wouldn’t claim one is universally better. The question is whether it helps with the things I actually do, and how much effort it takes to get a useful answer.

r001.rationale: The response says Gemini might be useful for technical questions, but it does not say Shunyu Yao’s everyday questions are predominantly technical or connect that to a preference for Gemini.

sol-6.1.text: For me, usefulness depends on the task. If I want to ask something quickly in Chinese or talk through an everyday problem, I’d judge Doubao by how naturally it fits that interaction. If I’m working through a technical question, I’d judge Gemini by whether it helps me reach a reliable answer. I wouldn’t reduce that to one being universally better. A model can be more capable overall and still be less useful for a particular person’s daily needs.
